harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 so every sudo command (with user and timestamp) is logged to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in (Defaults logfile, !syslog), verified it no longer appears in the general system log (/var/log/secure), then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id, and re-verified the logging configuration and behavior persisted post-reboot.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: OS (CentOS Stream 10), sudo 1.9.17p2, no existing sudoers.d drop-ins, rsyslog routing authpriv.* to /var/log/secure, boot_id fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34
Captured baseline tail of /var/log/secure showing sudo COMMAND= entries landing there prior to the change
Created /var/log/sudo-commands.log (mode 600, root:root)
Installed /etc/sudoers.d/95-sudo-command-logging with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log, Defaults log_year, Defaults !syslog; validated with visudo -cf (parsed OK)

Ran sudo whoami/id/cat and confirmed entries with user+timestamp appeared in /var/log/sudo-commands.log while no new COMMAND= lines appeared in /var/log/secure (only unrelated PAM session open/close lines, which carry no command detail)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, sudoers.d file presence, log line count
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1 (single node, acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned (two timeouts, then success)
Verified changed boot_id (fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34 -> 09b5da90-1817-400e-9c89-08300ef0be11) proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart: confirmed sudoers.d file persisted, ran new sudo commands, verified they logged to sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp and were absent as COMMAND= entries from /var/log/secure, confirmed rsyslog active

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: sudoers.d drop-in created and validated (visudo parsed OK); sudo-commands.log then shows entries like 'Sep 4 23:15:24 2026 : root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' with full timestamp, user, and command.

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries kept out of the general system log (/var/log/secure)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure before the change; after installing the !syslog / logfile sudoers Defaults, new sudo invocations (whoami, id, cat) no longer produced COMMAND= entries in /var/log/secure -- only generic PAM session open/close lines remained there.

evidence.requirement: Baseline health capture prior to restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, confirmed sudoers.d file present, rsyslog active, and log had 20 entries before reboot.
systemctl reboot issued in background with disown; command stream closed as node1 began shutting down, confirming the reboot was accepted and executing.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts/resets, exec access returned with boot_id 09b5da90-1817-400e-9c89-08300ef0be11, differing from the pre-restart fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, proving a genuine reboot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo command logging and cluster/service state on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers.d/95-sudo-command-logging still present, rsyslog active, and new sudo commands (whoami, tail) appended correctly-formatted entries to sudo-commands.log (25 lines, up from 20) while /var/log/secure tail showed no COMMAND= lines for them -- confirming the logging behavior survived the restart.

attempts.summary: Configured node1 so every sudo command (with user and timestamp) is logged to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in (Defaults logfile, !syslog), verified it no longer appears in the general system log (/var/log/secure), then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id, and re-verified the logging configuration and behavior persisted post-reboot.
